Agenda

1. The need

AI feels digital, but data centers create local energy, water, noise, and land-use pressure.

2. Our solution

A benefit show where the value is unmistakably human: live performance, community storytelling, and direct aid.

3. The pitch

Artists, budget, timeline, fundraising model, and measurable community impact.

Hook → Problem → Solution → Plan → Ask
The need

The cloud has a local footprint.

AI data centers concentrate huge electricity demand and cooling needs into specific neighborhoods. The benefits are global; the burdens can become local.

⚡

Energy strain

High, continuous electricity demand can crowd local grid capacity.

💧

Water strain

Some cooling systems rely on water in already stressed regions.

🔊

Noise & quality of life

Backup systems, cooling equipment, and industrial siting can affect residents.

Our lens: local residents, farmers, and communities near infrastructure

Our principle

Every ticket becomes a visible transfer from digital convenience back to physical communities.

We are not against AI. We are for repair.

Our project turns live, human performance into a practical support system for neighborhoods affected by the infrastructure behind AI.

awarenessdirect aidcommunity voicetransparent giving
Project design
Before the show

Community brief

Short documentary visuals explain one affected community: what is happening, who is impacted, and where donations go.

During the show

Human-only performance

No AI-generated music. The selling point is live skill, improvisation, risk, and presence.

After the show

Transparent aid

Donations support relief such as noise mitigation, water resilience, energy-bill assistance, or local advocacy partners.

Working title: Resonance Relief Benefit Series

Case focus

Different places, different pressure points.

The same AI boom can appear as an electricity issue in Dublin, a water issue in Arizona, and a neighborhood quality-of-life issue in Virginia.

Scores are presentation shorthand based on researched focus areas
Revenue model
01
Analogue & eco-merchandise

Vinyl-style posters, risograph prints, reusable bottles, seed paper, recycled cotton shirts.

02
ESG sponsors & matching grants

Companies match audience donations while gaining measurable community-impact reporting.

03
Global livestream donations

Pay-what-you-want stream with recurring donation prompts and transparent live total.

Goal: diversify income so aid is not dependent on one sponsor

Budget logic

We budget first, then donate transparently.

A benefit show still has real costs: venue, sound, insurance, security, artist travel, livestream, and promotion.

Venue + staff
$18k
Production / backline
$14k
Artists + travel
$16k
Marketing + design
$8k
Livestream + platform
$7k

Draft model only. Final version requires real venue and vendor quotes.

Financial credibility increases sponsor trust
Timeline

Six-month launch plan

Month 1

Confirm target community, aid partner, venue options.

Month 2

Artist outreach, sponsor deck, budget quotes.

Month 3

Launch campaign, teaser visuals, donation page.

Month 4-5

Ticket sales, community storytelling, press outreach.

Month 6

Benefit show, livestream, publish impact report.

Launch target: Earth Week or a local community date

$

👥

In-person attendance, livestream viewers, press/social reach, QR scans.

✓
Community validation

Partner feedback: Were needs represented accurately? Did support reach the right place?

Impact is not only money; it is money + attention + accountability
The ask

Would you sponsor this?

We are asking for a founding sponsor to cover production costs, match donations, and help publish a transparent community-impact report.
